places.name: Gulmarg
places.summary: Kashmir's 'meadow of flowers': India's best-known ski slopes in winter, wildflower meadows in summer, and the gondola to Apharwat.
places.seoTitle: Gulmarg Travel Guide: Gondola, Skiing & Meadows
places.seoDescription: Plan a Gulmarg trip: gondola stages and hours, skiing and the March winter festival, summer meadows, Alpather Lake, Kashmiri food and current travel advice.

images.alt: Gulmarg's meadows and pine forest below snow peaks

overview.text:
Gulmarg, the 'meadow of flowers', lies 60 km from Srinagar, about an hour and a half by car, in the Pir Panjal range. Kings from Yousuf Shah Chak to the Mughal emperor Jahangir came here, and so did the British.

In winter the snow turns it into Kashmir's skiing capital, with snowboarding, heli-skiing and tobogganing. In summer its meadows bloom with wildflowers such as edelweiss and lilies. The two-stage gondola climbs from the resort to Kongdori and up to about 12,300 ft on Apharwat.

The UK government currently advises against all travel to Jammu and Kashmir. Read the safety section before planning.

best_time.text: Winter, roughly December to March, is ski season, when Gulmarg is under snow. White Christmas and New Year are celebrated here, and a three-day Gulmarg Winter Festival takes place in March. In summer the meadows bloom, and it's the time for pony rides, golf at 2,650 m and walks up to Khilanmarg. The gondola runs roughly 10 am–5 pm, depending on the weather at both stages.

local_transport.text: Gulmarg is small and walkable. Ponies carry visitors to Khilanmarg (4 km from the bus stop), Strawberry Valley and Leopard Valley, and in summer up towards Alpather Lake. The gondola is the way up the mountain: about 9 minutes to Kongdori and 12 more to the second stage. Taxis come up from Srinagar and Tangmarg.

places.name: Alpather Lake
places.summary: High lake at the foot of Apharwat (4,200 m), frozen in winter and reached in summer from the gondola's upper stage.
places.seoTitle: Alpather Lake, Gulmarg: The Frozen Lake
places.seoDescription: Alpather Lake lies at 4,200 m at the foot of Apharwat above Gulmarg, frozen through winter and ringed by green in summer when the snow melts.

images.alt: Alpather Lake partly frozen below the snowy slopes of Apharwat

overview.text:
Alpather Lake sits at the base of the Apharwat peaks above Gulmarg, at about 4,200 m. It changes with the seasons. Frozen through winter, it has earned the nickname 'the Frozen Lake'; in summer, when the snow retreats, it is ringed by green. From up here you look down over the whole Gulmarg valley.

Visitors reach it in summer from the gondola's upper stations or by pony from Gulmarg via Kongdori. At this altitude, go slowly and turn back if the weather closes in.

items.body: Go only in good weather, and carry warm layers and water.
Start early so you can be back down before the gondola closes.

overview.text:
The Maharani Temple, with its distinctive red roof, sits on a small hillock in the middle of Gulmarg. It is said to be the royal temple of the Dogra dynasty and is dedicated to Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. Because it is raised above the meadow, it can be seen from all over Gulmarg, which makes it one of the resort's best-known landmarks.

It is a short walk from the main market and pairs well with a visit to St Mary's Church near the golf course.

items.body: Remove shoes and dress modestly inside.
The hillock is a good spot for photos of the meadow at either end of the day.

overview.text:
In winter, Gulmarg is covered in snow and becomes a skier's paradise. Its natural slopes are a challenge even for expert skiers. Beyond skiing there is snowboarding, heli-skiing (flying up by helicopter before the descent), snow scooters and tobogganing. The gondola carries skiers up Apharwat to about 12,293 ft.

The winter season brings White Christmas and New Year celebrations, and the three-day Gulmarg Winter Festival takes place in March.

items.body: Ski the upper mountain only with a qualified guide and avalanche awareness.
Book equipment and instructors in advance in peak weeks.
